A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StAR: Segment Anything Reasoner. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original StAR benchmark evaluations, component ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds robotics grounding evaluation, threshold sensitivity results and further case analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage GRPO/LoRA training, tiered mask reward, REST selection, label prediction and mask-clustering majority voting remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and additional evaluations do not establish a modified algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds zero-shot robotics spatial referring on RefSpatial-Bench's Location and Unseen sets (Table 3), including multi-anchor relations, hierarchical references and implied placements. This extends task coverage beyond the retained reasoning/referring segmentation benchmarks. Training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DPAD, SegCompass, DR2Seg, Seg-ReSearch and RSAgent to the reported comparisons. DPAD was previously discussed but lacked a comparison row. The new RefSpatial evaluation also compares against Gemini-2.5-Pro and RoboRefer-8B, substantially expanding comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce robotics success-rate reporting, an IoU clustering-threshold sweep from 0.70 to 0.90, and a Qwen3-VL 8B configuration for SAM 3 Agent. Existing training settings and segmentation protocols remain unchanged. Appendix A inconsistently retains its statement that Qwen3-VL SAM 3 Agent comparisons are excluded.

E4.justification: V2 adds threshold sensitivity (Table S.8), a with/without-REST Sudoku case (Fig. S.3), and dedicated failure analysis (Appendix I). Table S.5 supplies finer breakdowns of the existing Fig. 4 ablations. The failure figure includes new examples and reuses the earlier calendar example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent evaluation-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new example's successful-rollout counts describe search outcomes, not a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Retained StAR benchmark scores are unchanged, but the reported evidence expands substantially through new comparator scores, robotics results, detailed retrofit breakdowns and threshold results. For example, Table 3 newly reports StAR-8B success rates of 62.00%/38.96% on Location/Unseen, versus RoboRefer-8B's 52.00%/37.66%.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, advantage normalization, piecewise mask reward and appendix voting formulas are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and central StAR, parallel-scaling and ReasonSeg-X contributions remain unchanged. The conclusion adds an explicit claim that design choices provide individual incremental gains and synergistic benefits in combination, modestly strengthening the stated benefits.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly acknowledges that label prediction harms Comparative/Relational performance. Appendix I explains persistent relational and multi-step reasoning failures and associated hallucination, motivating verification and self-correction. These add concrete qualifications to the retained positive interpretations.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, prompt templates, training hyperparameters, hardware, training times and the repository link remain unchanged. The added robotics comparison does not supply corresponding detailed implementation or evaluation instructions.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for RSAgent, DR2Seg, Seg-ReSearch, SegCompass, AnchorSeg, DGSeg and RoboRefer, including a brief description of concurrent DGSeg. The existing positioning around RLVR bottlenecks and parallel versus sequential scaling remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: Localized expansions clarify majority voting and training/inference alignment. V2 adds a robotics-results passage, failure-analysis section, acknowledgments and author-affiliation information while preserving the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 1, adds Tables 3, S.5 and S.8, and adds the REST and failure-case figures. Existing figures and tables are largely retained and renumbered or relocated; the supplementary title page is reformatted.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons, threshold sensitivity and explicit failure and label-prediction tradeoffs improve empirical context and transparency. These strengthen an already extensive evaluation without changing the established method or results. Benefits are limited by sparse documentation of the robotics evaluation and the unresolved contradiction between Table 1's added Qwen3-VL SAM 3 Agent row and Appendix A's exclusion statement.
